home-remodeling.local_heading: Where Broward still has elbow room
intro_paragraphs: Plantation Acres runs between Hiatus Road and Flamingo Road, north of the North New River Canal, and it is the part of Broward that never got carved into quarter-acre lots. Most parcels here are an acre or larger. The houses sitting on them are a mixed bag: long single-story ranches from the late sixties and seventies, eighties customs with vaulted great rooms, and newer estate builds around Melaleuca Isles, Plantation Isles and Plantation Acres Estates. Owners buy the land first. Then they rebuild the house inside it.

The City of Plantation's Department of Building Safety issues the permit, with drawings submitted for electronic plan review through the city's own portal. Out here there is a step ahead of that: work in the Acres usually needs the Plantation Acres Improvement District's approval stamp before the city takes the application. Above both sits something contractors from Miami-Dade have to learn: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code countywide, publishes Broward's amendments, certifies building officials and inspectors, and issues formal interpretations when a section is disputed. Broward also sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every new window and door needs HVHZ product approval.

Two decades of South Florida work and more than 150 remodels and additions behind us, all permitted and inspected. On an acre you get something rare in this county: room to stage material, park a container and keep the crew out of a neighbor's sightline. We use it. The scope is priced and signed before anything comes down, a supervisor is on site every day, finished surfaces get covered rather than apologized for, and a single team owns the job from the first estimate through the last inspection and into the warranty period. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.

faqs.q: Who issues the building permit for a Plantation Acres remodel?
faqs.a: The City of Plantation. Its Department of Building Safety handles plan review, permit issuance and inspections inside city limits, and the Acres is city, not unincorporated Broward. Applications go in digitally through the city's own online portal. What surprises people is the step before it: in almost every case the Plantation Acres Improvement District wants its approval stamp first, so you go to the district before you go to City Hall. We file the whole sequence and track it.

faqs.q: What is the Board of Rules and Appeals, and does it affect my house?
faqs.a: Not directly, and that is rather the point. The Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code across the county: it publishes Broward's local amendments, certifies building officials, inspectors and plans examiners, hears appeals of a building official's decision, and issues formal interpretations of disputed code language. You will never sit in front of it. Your contractor should know it exists, because it is why Broward inspections have their own character.

faqs.q: Our house is on septic. Does that limit a whole-home remodel?
faqs.a: It limits how casually you add fixtures. Replacing what already exists is straightforward. Adding bedrooms, a second primary bath or a guest suite changes the design flow the system has to handle, and that gets reviewed by the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, which still runs septic permitting and inspection under the state onsite sewage program. We look at the tank, the drainfield location and the available yard early, before a floor plan assumes something the ground will not support.

faqs.q: Should we rent somewhere during a full remodel?
faqs.a: On an acre, more often than you could in a city-lot house, because we can wall off a wing and keep a working kitchen and bath alive while the other half is open. Full-gut scopes with the ceilings out are a different story. Most Acres clients move out for the loud middle and come back for finishes. We settle the phasing before demolition and put it in the schedule, not in a text message halfway through.

faqs.q: How much should we budget for a full gut in the Acres?
faqs.a: Square footage out here is generous, which is the honest first answer: a 4,500-square-foot ranch costs more to gut than a compact bungalow at any finish level. Beyond that it depends on how much mechanical, roof and structural work you take on at once. We put it in writing with allowances that reflect actual selections, rather than an opening number engineered to win the job and grow afterward. PGX is a high-end builder and rarely the cheapest bid; what you get instead is a number that holds.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Renovation in Plantation Acres, FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling for Plantation Acres homes: big rooms, closed galley layouts opened up, permits through the City of Plantation. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: The ranch kitchen, finally opened up
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Made-to-measure cabinetry, natural stone and the structural work that opens a closed galley into the great room, for Plantation Acres kitchens. Permitted through the city, run by a licensed contractor with a supervisor on site daily.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: A galley kitchen in a big house
intro_paragraphs: Plantation Acres has a particular kitchen problem. Houses here are large. Plenty of ranches from the seventies and eighties run four thousand square feet and up, yet the kitchen inside them is a closed galley with a pass-through to a formal dining room nobody has eaten in since 2004. Owners along Old Hiatus Road and NW 118th Avenue are rarely adding square footage. They are reclaiming it: pulling the wall to the family room, absorbing a dated breakfast nook, and setting a twelve-foot island where the peninsula used to sulk.

Kitchen remodeling in Plantation Acres is permitted by the City of Plantation, with electronic plan review and separate trade inspections for plumbing, electrical and mechanical. Two local wrinkles matter. Enlarge or add a window over the sink and the replacement unit needs a High-Velocity Hurricane Zone product approval, because Broward carries the same HVHZ requirements as Miami-Dade. And where a house sits on an onsite septic system rather than city sewer, adding a second dishwasher, a prep sink and a wet bar is worth reviewing before it is drawn rather than after.

PGX builds kitchens in the order that keeps them straight: cabinetry ordered early, structure opened and inspected, boxes set level, then stone templated against the real installation instead of a drawing. The scope is written and signed before the first cabinet leaves the wall, someone from PGX is here every working day, and the rest of your house gets sealed off rather than swept up afterward. More than twenty years working in South Florida, over 150 remodels and additions completed, none of them unpermitted.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: How an Acres kitchen comes together
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Written down and priced before a single cabinet comes off the wall. These five elements carry most of the budget and nearly all of the schedule risk.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry cut to the wall
scope_items.desc: Cabinet runs scaled to the nine and ten-foot ceilings out here, finished for humidity, and drawn to the wall instead of trimmed down from a stock line.

scope_items.desc: Big slabs measured in the room rather than off a drawing, over island framing engineered for the load, with seating overhangs carried on steel.

scope_items.desc: Beam design, sealed calculations and permitted structural work where block separates the kitchen from the great room it should have joined a decade ago.

scope_items.name: Appliance loads and panels

scope_items.name: Drainage and the septic question
scope_items.desc: Rerouted waste and vent lines for the new layout, plus a candid look at whether added fixtures belong on the existing onsite system.

faqs.q: Does the City of Plantation require a permit for a kitchen remodel?
faqs.a: For anything past paint and pulls, yes. Moving plumbing, adding circuits, changing ventilation and cutting into structure each require permits and inspections through the City of Plantation, and a genuine kitchen remodel does all four. Swapping cabinets into existing rough-ins is the exception. Unpermitted kitchen work has a habit of surfacing during a sale or an insurance inspection, and unwinding it later costs considerably more than the permit ever would.

faqs.q: Can I put an island in a 1970s Acres ranch with a wall in the way?
faqs.a: Usually. Block-and-truss houses from that era are cooperative once an engineer looks at them: a beam takes the load, new posts or filled cells carry it down, and the footing gets verified. Sealed drawings go in with the permit application, and the structural inspection happens before drywall. Taking the wall out is rarely the difficult part. Knowing exactly what to put back, and where, is the part worth paying for.

faqs.q: Our house is on well water. Does that affect a new kitchen?
faqs.a: It can. In Broward, water wells twelve inches in diameter or smaller are permitted through the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, and in the Acres they are most often irrigation wells rather than the potable supply. If any kitchen water does come off a well, test hardness and iron before you install a steam oven, a filtered pot filler or a clear-ice machine. Treatment is inexpensive. Replacing a scaled-up appliance is not.

faqs.q: How long does a custom kitchen take?
faqs.a: Cabinetry sets the clock. Custom packages take months to build, so we order at contract signing and schedule demolition around the delivery date rather than the reverse. On-site construction typically runs several weeks to a couple of months, longer when a structural opening or a relocated range is in the scope. Anyone promising a finished custom kitchen in three weeks is quoting stock boxes and hoping you will not notice.

faqs.q: How much is a proper kitchen out here?
faqs.a: Cabinetry, stone and appliances set the range, and Acres kitchens tend to be physically large, which pushes linear footage and therefore cost. We price against a written specification after a walk-through, so you are comparing a real number to a real scope. PGX works at the high end and does not bid to be the cheapest name on the list. We bid to deliver the version that does not get quietly stripped down in month three.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_heading: Show us the kitchen you tolerate
kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: One walk-through, one honest conversation about how you actually cook, and you get a priced scope on paper, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Plantation Acres, FL Bathroom Remodeling | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Primary suite and guest bathroom remodeling in Plantation Acres, FL — stone, frameless glass, waterproofing tested before tile. Estimates at (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Primary suites carved out of spare rooms
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Guest baths and primary suites throughout Plantation Acres: freestanding tubs, frameless glass, stone, and waterproofing proved with a flood test. Permitted by the City of Plantation and run by a licensed, insured contractor with a supervisor on site.
bathroom-remodeling.local_heading: Four bathrooms, none of them right
intro_paragraphs: A 1978 house in Plantation Acres often has four bathrooms and no primary suite. The arithmetic was different then: a compartment toilet, a fiberglass tub-shower, a four-foot vanity, and a closet sized for a coat rack. What owners in Melaleuca Isles, Plantation Acres Estates and the older sections along NW 118th Avenue do now is annex the adjoining bedroom or an oversized hall closet, build one genuine suite, and then bring the guest baths up to the same standard so the house reads as one house instead of four decades.

Bathroom permits come from the City of Plantation, and the plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections happen before anything gets closed in. The Acres adds two considerations most Broward neighborhoods skip entirely. Where a home runs on an onsite septic system rather than city sewer, increasing fixture count gets reviewed by the Florida Department of Health in Broward County, which handles septic permitting and inspection here. And any new or enlarged bathroom window needs an HVHZ product approval, since Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone.

No room punishes shortcuts faster, so we build it in the right order and prove the parts nobody will ever see. Pans get filled and left to sit overnight before a single tile is set. Slopes are checked with a level. Heavy glass hangs on blocking installed while the wall was open, not on a hope and a toggle bolt. The scope is written and signed, a PGX supervisor is here every working day, and the route from your front door to the work gets covered. Insured, and licensed as CGC1539072, with every project on this list permitted and inspected.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Written down before the tile is ordered, because a change made after the waterproofing goes in is not a change. It is a redo.

scope_items.desc: Combining a bedroom, a hall bath and closet space into one primary suite, with layout, rough-ins and permit drawings handled as a single package.

scope_items.desc: Recessed pans and linear drains cut into slab-on-grade where structure allows, water-tested before tile, and a shallow curb where the slab honestly will not cooperate.

scope_items.name: Freestanding tubs, supported
scope_items.desc: Tub placement checked against floor structure and drain location first, then stone and tile surfaces sealed to survive daily use in Broward humidity.

scope_items.name: Old pipe, gone for good
scope_items.desc: Replacing galvanized supply and tired cast iron while the walls stand open, which is the only moment in this house's life when it is cheap.

scope_items.desc: Bigger rooms need bigger fans, so we size them and duct them out through the roof, then light the mirror from both sides instead of overhead.

faqs.q: Does a new bathroom mean a bigger drainfield?
faqs.a: It might, and there is an actual process behind that question rather than an opinion. Onsite systems are sized to a design flow tied to bedroom count and fixtures, and changes are permitted and inspected through the Florida Department of Health in Broward County. Sometimes the existing tank and drainfield absorb the new load without complaint. Sometimes the system needs modification or replacement, and learning that during design is dramatically better than learning it during framing.

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels in Plantation need permits?
faqs.a: Anything that moves a drain, changes a vent, alters wiring or touches structure does. The City of Plantation reviews the drawings and inspects the rough-in before it is covered, which is the part that protects you: somebody other than your contractor confirmed the waterproofing and plumbing before tile hid them. Cosmetic swaps such as paint, a mirror or a fixture on an existing box do not. We handle the filings and the inspection scheduling.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a 1970s slab house?
faqs.a: Frequently, and it depends entirely on what is under the tile. On slab-on-grade we saw and recess the pan area, reroute the drain and confirm there is enough fall to the existing line. Where the slab is too thin or the drain sits in the wrong place, a half-inch curb over a correctly pitched pan does the same job and photographs nearly identically. We check the structure before you commit to the look.

faqs.q: How long will we be without the primary bath?
faqs.a: Plan on several weeks for a straightforward gut and rebuild, longer when structure moves, custom glass is involved or stone has to be fabricated. Waterproofing and mortar beds need genuine cure time, and rushing them is how leaks get born. In an Acres house there is usually a spare bath to live on, which takes pressure off the calendar and lets the work be done properly rather than quickly.

faqs.q: What does a high-end primary bath cost?
faqs.a: Stone, glass and fixtures move the number most, followed by whatever is behind the wall: new drains, a relocated stack, a rebuilt floor. We scope after walking the space and tell you what the building needs before you fall for a tile. We are not the low bid, and we do not price a project on the quiet assumption that change orders will make up the difference later.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Point at the room that annoys you every single morning. We will scope it honestly and quote it in writing, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Acreage Home Additions, Plantation Acres FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Rear extensions, second stories and in-law suites in Plantation Acres, FL — acreage setbacks, septic and drainage planned first. Talk to PGX at (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Additions the lot can actually take
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, guest houses and garage conversions in Plantation Acres, engineered for the lot, coordinated with septic and drainage, permitted by the City of Plantation, with a licensed contractor and a daily supervisor.
home-additions.local_heading: An acre is not automatically buildable
intro_paragraphs: Additions make more sense in Plantation Acres than almost anywhere else in Broward, because the land is already yours. A seventies ranch on a one-acre parcel off Old Hiatus Road can take a rear great room, a detached guest house or a second floor without crowding a thing. The briefs repeat themselves: a primary wing with its own entrance, an in-law suite for parents moving down from the north, a garage bay long enough for the boat, and studios or workshops the original builder never contemplated.

The City of Plantation permits the work, but an addition here involves more than a permit application. Parts of the Acres carry the city's rural estate zoning, which is why horses and outbuildings are contemplated at all and why setbacks and lot coverage behave differently than in a platted subdivision. The Plantation Acres Improvement District maintains the canals, culverts and pump stations draining roughly 2,000 acres out here, reviews permits ahead of the city, and holds easements along its banks that a footprint has to respect. Add tree removal permits and, on septic properties, drainfield location, and the site plan matters as much as the floor plan.

The half of an addition budget nobody photographs is the half we care most about: footings tied into a forty-year-old foundation, tie-beams and truss connections that satisfy Broward's amendments to the Florida Building Code, and a roof tie-in that will not telegraph a seam in five years. More than 150 remodels and additions built over two decades in South Florida, none of them without a permit. A written scope you sign, one supervisor who does not rotate off, and the same team answering for the job from the first sketch through the final inspection.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition starts with a survey, an engineer and a hard look at where the drainfield and the easements sit. Then we draw.

scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites pushed out into the yard, with the footings, tie-beams and roof connection detailed by an engineer and permitted in a single set.

scope_items.name: A separate guest house
scope_items.desc: Separate suites and casitas the rural estate zoning here can accommodate, with utilities, septic capacity and setbacks confirmed before anyone draws an elevation.

scope_items.name: Garages, barns and workshops
scope_items.desc: Deep garages, equipment barns and workshops built on acreage, engineered for wind load and detailed so they look intentional from the road rather than improvised.

scope_items.name: Foundations and underpinning
scope_items.desc: New footings, steel, filled cells and tie-beam work: nobody photographs any of it, and it decides whether the addition ages with the house or against it.

faqs.q: Can I build a detached guest house on my Plantation Acres lot?
faqs.a: Often yes, and the Acres is one of the few places in Broward where that question is realistic rather than wishful. Parts of the neighborhood carry the city's rural estate zoning, which contemplates outbuildings, animals and accessory structures on larger parcels. What decides it is your specific zoning designation, lot size, setbacks, lot coverage and, on septic properties, whether the onsite system and available yard can serve another dwelling. We verify zoning and survey before you spend on design.

faqs.q: How does the Plantation Acres Improvement District affect my addition?
faqs.a: It affects where you build, not whether you build, and it usually reviews your permit before the city does. PAID began in 1963 as the Dixie Drainage District and was reconstituted under its current name in 1982. It maintains the canals, culverts and pump stations draining roughly 2,000 acres between Hiatus and Flamingo Roads. Canal-adjacent lots typically carry drainage easements, and filling, paving or building across one is a poor thing to discover at plan review. We confirm easements and grades off the survey during design.

faqs.q: Will an addition force us onto a bigger septic system?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Bedrooms are the usual trigger, because onsite system sizing keys off bedroom count and estimated flow rather than raw square footage. A great room extension may not touch it at all. A three-bedroom wing with two baths very likely will. Modifications and replacements are permitted and inspected through the Florida Department of Health in Broward County. We raise the question during schematic design so the answer becomes a line item instead of an ambush.

faqs.q: How long will the whole process take?
faqs.a: Front-load your expectations. Survey, design, structural engineering, zoning verification and city plan review commonly consume several months before ground breaks, and that is before septic or drainage coordination. Construction then adds several months of its own, driven by size and by whether you are going up rather than out. For a substantial addition, a year from first conversation to furniture is a realistic frame. We put the whole sequence in writing so no phase is a mystery.

faqs.q: Should we add on, or just buy something bigger?
faqs.a: If you like your acre, usually. Land like this is finite in Broward, and most of the Acres has no homeowner association at all, though a handful of the smaller platted subdivisions inside it do. You keep the lot, the canopy and the address, and you buy exactly the rooms you are missing rather than inheriting somebody else's compromises. It is still months of real construction and real permitting, so it pays off for people intending to stay put. We read the feasibility honestly before you spend on drawings.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send over the survey and whatever you have in mind. Zoning, septic, drainage and real numbers get settled before anyone draws, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Pavilions & Summer Kitchens, Plantation Acres FL | PGX
outdoor-living.meta_description: Plantation Acres estates get engineered pavilions, plumbed summer kitchens, terraces and driveways. Licensed GC, permits pulled. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered pavilions, pool terraces and long driveways for Plantation Acres properties, engineered for Broward wind loads, permitted through the City of Plantation, and delivered by a licensed, insured contractor who shows up.
outdoor-living.local_heading: You bought the acre for this
intro_paragraphs: Nobody buys an acre in Plantation Acres for the interior. They buy it for what sits behind the house, then spend a decade not using it. The outdoor living projects that fix that tend to be substantial: a covered pavilion with a working summer kitchen, a pool deck that runs out toward a district canal in Melaleuca Isles, a run-in shed and paddock fencing, a circular drive that keeps guests off the swale. Plantation was founded on the idea of one-acre lots meant for growing things. Out here that idea survived.

A backyard build in Plantation Acres touches more agencies than people expect. The City of Plantation permits the structures and the trade work, and its landscape division issues tree removal and relocation permits under the city ordinance, which runs alongside Broward County's tree preservation rules. Canal-side lots sit inside the Plantation Acres Improvement District, whose maintenance easements and canal banks are not places to pour a slab. New exterior openings need HVHZ product approvals, and pavilion connections have to be engineered for Broward wind loads rather than assembled from a kit off a pallet.

We build exterior work to the same standard as the inside of the house. Gas, water and electrical runs to a summer kitchen get permitted and inspected rather than buried and forgotten. Pavilion footings are engineered and uplift connections are drawn by somebody who stamped them. Grading is planned so an August storm sheds toward the swale instead of the family room. A written scope you approve, someone from PGX here every working day, and a crew that hauls its debris out instead of letting an acre quietly absorb it.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One project, one permit set, one crew, whether the yard needs a single pavilion or a full rebuild from the back door to the fence line.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens under the pavilion
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and electrical out to the pavilion, weather-rated cabinetry and counters, and vent hoods sized for the grill you actually bought.

scope_items.name: Pavilions and pergolas, engineered
scope_items.desc: Covered structures with designed footings and uplift connections, detailed to pick up the roof pitch and fascia of the house instead of merely standing beside it.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and terraces
scope_items.desc: Resurfacing and expanding pool decks with drainage resolved first, so the terrace sheds water toward the swale rather than back against the slab.

scope_items.name: Driveways, gates and fencing
scope_items.desc: Long approach drives, circular turnarounds, paddock and estate fencing, and entry gates, coordinated with district easements and city right-of-way requirements.

scope_items.name: Stucco, paint and openings
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration, color changes and impact-rated door and window replacement, so the front of the house catches up with whatever just happened out back.

faqs.q: Does a pavilion and summer kitchen need permits out here?
faqs.a: Yes, and more than one. The covered structure takes a building permit with engineered drawings; the gas, plumbing and electrical runs are each permitted and inspected separately by the City of Plantation. A grill on a rolling cart does not. The difference shows up at resale and at claim time, and an unpermitted attached structure is precisely the thing an insurer notices when you most need them not to.

faqs.q: Can I build right up to the canal behind my house?
faqs.a: No, and this is where a current survey earns its fee. Canal-side properties in Plantation Acres fall inside the Plantation Acres Improvement District, which maintains the canals, culverts and pump stations for the whole neighborhood and holds easements along the banks for access and maintenance. Slabs, footings and permanent structures inside an easement are a problem you do not want to solve after the truck leaves. We locate the easement line during design and set the footprint back from it.

faqs.q: There are big trees where the pavilion should go. What now?
faqs.a: You need a permit before anything comes down, and possibly mitigation planting. The City of Plantation issues tree removal and relocation permits through its landscape division, and Broward County's tree preservation ordinance operates alongside the city rules. Mature canopy on an acre is worth more than the two weeks of schedule it costs to design around it, and shifting a footprint eight feet is usually cheaper than replacement trees. We price both routes.

faqs.q: Will a summer kitchen and pool deck survive out here?
faqs.a: If it is specified honestly. The Acres is inland, so salt is a smaller problem than it is in Lighthouse Point or along the Intracoastal, but heat, ultraviolet and a five-month rainy season are relentless. We use stainless rated for outdoor service, dense stone sealed properly, powder-coated or marine-grade hardware, and drainage that genuinely moves water. Big-box outdoor cabinetry swells and delaminates in a single Florida summer.

faqs.q: What does a full backyard project cost?
faqs.a: It scales with structure and utilities far more than with square footage. A resurfaced pool deck is one conversation. A roofed pavilion carrying a summer kitchen, gas, water, power and a pool bath is an entirely different one, with engineering and several trade permits behind it. Appliance and stone choices then swing the total as hard as the footprint does. We walk the property, scope it in writing, and let you compare real specifications.

outdoor-living.cta_heading: Bring us out to the backyard
outdoor-living.cta_sub: Show us the acre and tell us what you want it to do. The scope and the number come back in writing, in English o en español.
